transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-09 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees listed above.

Summary (auto): Quick readout from the pilot, then handoff to procurement/legal to move toward a signed MSA and pilot-to-prod plan.

00:00 Maya (AE): okay, hi everyone, thanks for making time. this is Maya from Redwood, with Carlos on the call, our solutions engineer, and Lena from CS. we wanted to run through the pilot readout, sync on redlines, and make sure procurement has what they need to move forward.
00:18 Ethan (Procurement): thanks, Maya. quick ask up front — can we keep this focused, we have a few schedule constraints; Olivia is dialing in after another call but she'll be here for the legal bits.
00:28 Maya: absolutely, we can prioritize those sections. Carlos, quick pilot highlights?
00:33 Carlos (SE): yeah, sure. so the two-week pilot ran on a dedicated pool, we routed demo workloads and production-like traffic. median latency was 85 ms for the shorter prompt set, p95 was 210 ms, p99 spikes correlated with cold-starts on a small set of hosts — we attached traces in the perf spreadsheet. there was also a caching behavior note: prefix/KV cache reduced token generation compute by roughly 28% on repeated prompts.
01:05 Priya (Head of ML Ops): that matches what our engineers saw, the p99 spikes were during the midday burst test. curious — the cold-start mitigation you mentioned, was that the container warmers or a model-variant fallback?
01:15 Carlos: mostly container warmers plus light warm pools we configured. we also exercised the fallback to a quantized model variant for heavy tails which kept latency within an acceptable range, albeit with a minor quality delta. my notes say the fallback rule was last-resort after 3s.
01:36 Samir (Security): quick interjection — how are you handling the keys for those quantized models? specifically KMS rotation?
01:42 Carlos: good call. for this pilot we used Redwood-managed keys in our hosted test harness, but in the private/Dedicated plan we support customer-managed KMS (HSM integrations), with rotation policies and audit logs. that is available in the private control plane.
01:58 Olivia (Legal) [joining]: sorry I'm late, can you recap the asks on the MSA/DPA?
02:05 Maya: sure. procurement wants the full bundle (MSA, DPA, SLA), we can send the standard templates and highlight the common redlines customers request — egress fees, data residency, and privileged keying paths. Ethan, do you have a target for redline return?
02:22 Ethan: we'd like first-pass internal review by next Friday, ideally with comments back the following Monday. our legal is small but quick.
02:30 Maya: perfect. we'll aim to get you the deck and redlines by Friday EOD.
02:35 Priya: on SLA, we need clarity on p99 latency SLO and the escalation matrix. our app is latency sensitive for user-facing features; if p99 exceeds 500 ms repeatedly we'll need automatic fallback to a cheaper hosted region. is that in the SLA?
02:50 Carlos: we can codify p99 targets in the SLA and include automatic fallback policies. our standard SLA has uptime percentages and credits; for latency SLOs we have threshold agreements plus canary/rollback policies. toggle note — the automatic fallback requires routing policies configured in the Console.
03:10 Olivia: on data protections — DPA needs explicit language around ephemeral logging and retention. also audit logs for token-level access. does Redwood provide token-level logging or is that opt-in?
03:25 Lena (CSM): it's opt-in and configurable; by default we don't persist full request payloads for hosted, but enterprise Dedicated/Private customers get extended audit logs, with retention set per tenant. we also have optional filtered logs for debug that exclude PII.
03:45 Samir: what's the network topology for Private? we're evaluating VPC peering vs on-prem airgapped instances. any limitations on egress?
03:55 Carlos: Private deployment supports VPC peering and a deployable appliance for air-gapped installs; egress is configurable — some customers choose to route model updates via a controlled mirror. there are operational differences; full on-prem requires additional maintenance windows and longer lead times.
04:18 Ethan: cost question — during the pilot we saw estimates that suggested committed capacity would be 40% cheaper unit-cost than burst. can you send the model showing committed vs on-demand pricing?
04:28 Maya: yes, I'll send a pricing breakdown. we'll include committed reserved pricing scenarios and a simple calculator based on your expected QPS and tokens per request.
04:36 Priya: success criteria for the pilot — from our side we defined: p95 & p99 latency thresholds, <0.2% model quality regression vs baseline for the quantized variant, and throughput of at least 120 rps sustained. we met p95 but close on p99. what's a reasonable remediation path?
04:55 Carlos: remediation options include increasing warm pool size, pinning more hosts for critical routes, or using autoscale policies with burst units. cost/latency tradeoffs are in the perf sheet. we can run a targeted p99 mitigation run in a focused pilot iteration.
05:20 Olivia: legally, we also need to lock the data residency clause — EU residency for EU customers. can Redwood commit to region isolation for tenant data?
05:31 Maya: yes, we support region isolation and can include a contractual clause for data residency in the DPA. for full Private deployments we can provide customer-controlled storage in region.
05:43 Samir: encryption at rest and in transit details — is TLS mutual authentication supported between customer infra and the Redwood control plane? and for KMS, do you support BYOK?
05:55 Carlos: mTLS is available for Dedicated and Private connectors; BYOK is supported with rotation schedules and audit hooks. for hosted, we offer Redwood-managed keys unless BYOK is requested and provisioned.
06:10 Ethan: procurement will push on indemnity caps and liability around model hallucinations and PII leakages — are those typical redline points?
06:22 Olivia: yes, and we'll need to see indemnity language and carveouts. also need vendor cyber insurance certificates — can you share SOC2 report and relevant pen test summaries?
06:33 Maya: we can share SOC 2 Type II and a summary of our most recent red team engagement; full reports are under NDA but we can provide whatever is needed for the gate.
06:42 Priya: one more technical — we used function-calling in a couple of flows; any limitations on structured output enforcement? we had one run where the model returned a slightly different schema.
06:56 Carlos: we have structured output tools and schema-checkers in the Console; for high-assurance flows we recommend the structured output + post-processor validator. we can help design the prompt set to avoid regressions.
07:12 Ethan: ok, sounds like we have the pieces. procurement's timeline: legal first pass by next Friday, commercial terms negotiation the week after, and a target signature by end of month if no major redlines.
07:26 Maya: that aligns with our expectations. for the pilot to prod transition we'll propose a short bridging contract — three-month reserved capacity that converts into annual commit on acceptance.
07:37 Olivia: about egress and export controls — need clear language on who bears export fees for model artifacts or derivative data when we move logs out.
07:48 Maya: we'll include egress fee paths and an escrow/transfer clause in the MSA appendix for heavy export scenarios.
07:57 Samir: can we set up a security deep-dive? we'd like the infra team to see network diagrams and KMS flows.
08:04 Maya: yes, we can schedule that the week after next; Carlos and our infra lead will present.
08:10 Priya: last note — do you have references in finance companies or fintech? procurement likes similar-industry references.
08:18 Maya: absolutely, we'll send a short reference list and case studies — a couple of fintech customers have private deployments.
08:24 Ethan: perfect. one more small logistics question — invoicing cadence for reserved commits? monthly or quarterly?
08:33 Maya: typically monthly with annual contracts; we can offer quarterly billing on request. will note that in the commercial template.
08:40 Olivia: thanks all. we'll review the MSA redlines and provide an initial set.
08:45 Maya: great. quick recap: Redwood to send MSA/DPA/SLA bundle + pricing and perf logs; schedule security deep-dive; Tesseract to decide pilot scope final and circulate stakeholders.
08:56 Lena: I'll attach the pilot perf spreadsheet link in the follow-up and include the trace files.
09:01 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc package and next meeting invites.

End transcript.

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional word swaps (e.g., 'cold starts' transcribed as 'cold carts'), speaker labels reassigned in one section, and timestamps approximate every 30-60s.
